cve_summary: Buffer overflow in hw/scsi-disk.c in the SCSI subsystem in QEMU before 0.15.2, as used by Xen, might allow local guest users with permission to access the CD-ROM to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted SAI READ CAPACITY SCSI command.  NOTE: this is only a vulnerability when root has manually modified certain permissions or ACLs.
commit_message:
scsi-disk: lazily allocate bounce buffer

It will not be needed for reads and writes if the HBA provides a sglist.
In addition, this lets scsi-disk refuse commands with an excessive
allocation length, as well as limit memory on usual well-behaved guests.

Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Creates a new SCSI request and defines properties for virtual SCSI devices.

Parameters: 
d (SCSIDevice*): Pointer to the SCSI device.
tag (uint32_t): Tag identifier for the request.
lun (uint32_t): Logical Unit Number for the request.
hba_private (void*): Pointer to private data for the host bus adapter.

Returns: 
SCSIRequest*: Pointer to the newly allocated SCSI request.

Logic: 
The function `scsi_new_request` allocates a new SCSI request using the provided device, tag, lun, and private data. It is used in the initialization of various virtual SCSI devices, including SCSI disks and CD-ROMs, which are defined in the `scsi_disk_info` array. Each device entry specifies its name, firmware name, description, size, reset function, initialization function, destruction function, and a property list that includes common properties defined by the macro `DEFINE_SCSI_DISK_PROPERTIES`.
